questions.prompt: According to your notes, put the steps of the classic TLS 1.2 handshake in order.
steps: The browser sends a hello listing the encryption methods it supports
The server replies with its hello and its certificate
The browser checks the certificate was signed by a trusted certificate authority
The browser and server agree on a session key
All further data is encrypted with the session key

evidence.quote: First, the browser sends a hello message listing the encryption methods it supports.
Finally, all further data is encrypted with that session key.

questions.explanation: Paragraph 5 gives the classic TLS 1.2 handshake in order. (TLS 1.3 shortens it; see paragraph 6.)

questions.prompt: According to your notes, what does the server send along with its hello message?

evidence.quote: the server replies with its own hello and its certificate
A private key is kept secret by the server.
After that, the browser and server agree on a session key.

questions.explanation: The server sends its certificate; its private key stays secret, and the session key is agreed later.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, three of these are protections TLS provides. Which one is not?
questions.categoryRule: TLS provides encryption, authentication and integrity.

evidence.quote: TLS provides three protections covered in these notes: encryption, authentication and integrity.
Anonymity is not one of these protections

questions.explanation: The website still sees your IP address, so HTTPS doesn't make you anonymous.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, connect each protection to what it means.

pairs.right: Others on the network can't read the data

evidence.quote: Encryption means others on the network cannot read the data.

pairs.right: You can check you're talking to the real website

evidence.quote: Authentication means you can check you are talking to the real website.

pairs.right: Changes in transit would be detected

evidence.quote: Integrity means the data cannot be changed in transit without it being detected.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, connect each item to its description.

evidence.quote: A public key can be shared openly.
A private key is kept secret by the server.

pairs.right: A trusted organisation that signs certificates

evidence.quote: A certificate authority is a trusted organisation that signs certificates.

pairs.right: A shared key that encrypts the rest of the conversation

evidence.quote: A session key is a shared key used to encrypt the rest of the conversation.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, which of these is kept secret by the server?

evidence.quote: A public key can be shared openly.
the server replies with its own hello and its certificate
A private key is kept secret by the server.

questions.explanation: Only the private key stays secret; the public key and certificate are shared.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, which port does HTTPS use by default?

evidence.quote: By default, HTTPS uses port 443, while plain HTTP uses port 80.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, in the newest version, how many round trips does the handshake usually need before encrypted data can flow?

evidence.quote: the handshake usually needs only one round trip

questions.explanation: Your notes say one round trip in TLS 1.3.

questions.prompt: According to your notes, what does the padlock icon in the address bar mean?

evidence.quote: A padlock icon in the address bar means the connection is encrypted.

options.text: The website is honest and safe
options.label: contradicted

evidence.quote: It does not mean the website itself is honest or safe.

options.text: You are anonymous to the website
options.label: contradicted

evidence.quote: the website still sees your IP address

questions.explanation: The padlock means encryption, not that the site is trustworthy or that you're anonymous.
